what: RBC Bearings makes precision bearings and engineered components: the parts that let aircraft control surfaces, landing gear and industrial machinery move accurately under load.
customers: Aircraft makers and their suppliers, defence contractors, and industrial machinery builders, often on long-term agreements.
money: bearings for aircraft structures, engines and defence systems
bearings and components for machinery, mining and energy equipment
moat: Parts qualified into an aircraft programme stay there for the life of the programme, because requalifying a bearing means recertifying the aircraft.
risks: 42 times earnings is a high price for an industrial supplier
Aerospace production rates depend on Boeing and Airbus, which have both missed delivery targets
$945M of debt against $57M of cash, from the Dodge acquisition
opportunities: Analysts see about 29% upside, with revenue up from $943M to $1.9B in four years
A 15.4% net margin and $399M of free cash flow, strong for a parts maker
Aircraft already flying need replacement bearings, an aftermarket that earns more than original equipment
watch: Aerospace bookings and whether the industrial half keeps growing alongside them.
